questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Which language is the easiest for adults to learn
How children learn their first language at school
Whether language-learning apps really help people learn
Why fictional languages are becoming popular
questions.why: Pippa says they'll try to answer whether apps like Duolingo, Babbel and Busuu really help.

questions.q: According to Pippa, what do many language apps say they focus on?
options: Learning through situations, not grammar rules
Long daily lessons with a live online teacher
Practising pronunciation with native speakers
Reading full novels in the new language
questions.why: She says many apps focus on language for situations and implicit learning, not directly teaching rules.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention how children learn their first language?
options: To show that children learn faster with apps
To give an example of learning without formal lessons
To argue that grammar lessons are useless
To explain why children dislike language classes
questions.why: He says children's learning is mostly implicit because 'they don't have lessons', then asks if this works for adults.

questions.q: What is Professor Liz Wonnacott's view on how adults learn languages?
options: They should copy children exactly and avoid grammar
They can easily achieve full immersion
They learn best only in classrooms
Some direct teaching of grammar and vocabulary helps them
questions.why: She says there is evidence that some explicit teaching of grammar and vocabulary is helpful.

questions.q: Who were the learners in the study that Liz found interesting?
options: Spanish speakers learning English in two ways
English speakers learning Spanish at home
Children learning several languages at once
Teachers testing different apps in class
questions.why: The study compared two groups of Spanish speakers learning English, one with an app and one in classes.

questions.q: What was the main result of that study?
options: Both groups improved in exactly the same way
Classroom learners did better in every test
App users did better in grammar, class in listening
App users improved more in listening tests
questions.why: Duolingo learners improved more in written grammar tests, classroom learners more in listening.

questions.q: Why does Liz say the study has limits?
options: It lasted for only one week in the summer
It looked at one language, one app, one school
Many learners did not finish the final tests
It was paid for by a large app company
questions.why: She says it's 'one particular language, in one particular app, against one particular school'.

questions.q: What do Liz and the presenters recommend in the end?
options: Stopping app use after the first few months
Using only apps, because they are convenient
Learning only through full immersion abroad
Mixing apps with human teaching and more
questions.why: Liz suggests combining human teaching with apps, and Neil suggests podcasts and speaking practice too.
